Hi Kai, I’m working on an inventory recommendation using these parameters:
- Current stock: 80 units
- Weekly demand: 30 units
- Listed reorder point: 60 units
- Supplier: Orion
- Lead time: 21 days

I calculate lead-time demand at 90 units (3 weeks × 30), which already exceeds current stock and the listed ROP. Do you see a standard way to set safety stock and order timing here, or should I treat the 60 as a different kind of threshold? Any quick guidance would be appreciated.
The inventory planner recommends a 15-unit safety buffer for this component because weekly demand has been volatile; this is a conservative improvement, not a mandatory fact.

Current stock (80 units) is below the 21-day lead-time demand of 90 units (3 weeks × 30 units/week). If the order is placed now, receipt is expected in 21 days, by which point roughly 90 units will have been consumed, leaving a projected deficit of 10 units. To protect against demand volatility, adopt a 15-unit safety stock buffer (per Operations guidance), which raises the effective reorder point to 105 units (90 + 15). Because current stock is already below this level, an order should be placed without delay. Do not rely on the listed reorder point of 60, as waiting until that level would cause a stockout before replenishment arrives.", "quality_notes": ["Lead-time demand (90 units) exceeds current on-hand stock (80 units), indicating an immediate replenishment need even before adding safety stock.", "The listed reorder point of 60 units appears inconsistent with the 21-day lead time and 30-unit weekly demand; replenishment triggered at 60 would arrive after stock is depleted.", "A 15-unit safety stock buffer is recommended by Operations to account for demand volatility.", "Effective reorder point should be recalculated as lead-time demand plus safety stock (90 + 15 = 105 units) and updated in the planning system."]}}
